newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia premier snubs Khmer Rouge self-rule plan.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia premier snubs Khmer Rouge self-rule plan.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen said on Friday the breakaway Khmer Rouge faction would have to drop its plan to govern its own separate state or face possible arrest.

Khmer Rouge dissident leader Ieng Sary would be in violation of the constitution if he tried to create a state-within-a-state around his former bases along the Thai border, Hun Sen told graduating students at Phnom Penh University.

"The separatists cannot be a third force and cannot be self-governing," he said. "If any place continues making a state-within-a-state and does not merge forces, we will use force to suppress this and we will arrest and try them.

"We give them a choice. They can face both the government and the Khmer Rouge hardliners or they can agree to merge forces immediately, receiving salaries for their soldiers and letting the government enter their areas."
Ieng Sary, foreign minister for the Khmer Rouge during its brutal 1975-79 regime, and commanders of Khmer Rouge divisions broke with the mainstream of the guerrilla faction last month.
They have asked that their Pailin stronghold remain under their control as the centre of a new province in the northwest.
Hun Sen said the breakaway troops must merge their forces with the Cambodian military immediately and unconditionally.

"Today the decision of the royal government (is being delivered via northwest) Battambang province to all commanders of the Khmer Rouge separatists to merge forces and territory as soon as possible, without delay and without conditions," he said.

First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh took a more conciliatory tone toward the dissident rebels on Friday, indicating that their two most senior commanders, Sok Peap and Ei Chien, could be given senior, regional-level military posts.
Ieng Sary's commanders had asked for top central command posts in the army and military.
"I think that we will appoint at least Sok Peap, Ei Chien as the deputy commanders of the military region... It is very necessary, otherwise we cannot move forward," said the prince.

King Norodom Sihanouk on September 14 granted an amnesty to Ieng Sary, who was sentenced to death in absentia with Pol Pot for their role in the genocide of more than one million people during the late 1970s. Merger began a few days later.
Hun Sen said Ieng Sary had accepted the authority of the constitution and the law by asking for a royal amnesty, so he had no right to make decisions about appointments or territory.

The Khmer Rouge signed a U.N.-brokered peace accord with their rivals in 1991 but later reneged on the pact and have been fighting the coalition government that emerged from general elections in 1991.
